name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Tim Kennedy running with large financial advantage ($2.3M raised)
Prediction markets price Kennedy at ~94% to win
No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The baseline model points to a ~21.5-point Democratic margin built on the district's D+11 lean, a favorable environment, incumbency, and Kennedy's dominant fundraising. With no contrary evidence and markets at 94% for Kennedy, I stay essentially at the baseline as Safe D.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-26 is a Buffalo-area district that leans Democratic by about 11 points, and incumbent Tim Kennedy is seeking reelection after winning the seat in a special election. He has raised over $2.3 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Dennis Hannon has reported minimal fundraising. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

The quantitative baseline projects a Democratic margin of roughly 21 points, combining the district lean, incumbency, money, and the national environment. Prediction markets give Kennedy about a 94% chance of winning. With no evidence pointing the other way, this race is rated Safe Democratic, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
